edges.description: The stem cells are proposed to give rise to the endothelium of the tumor. Shown for human cells implanted in mice; the step has not been observed in a child.
The fat that replaces the tumor is proposed to come from the same stem cells. Shown for human cells implanted in mice.
With little VEGFR1 to hold VEGF back, VEGF reaches VEGFR2 and keeps it active.
Active VEGFR2 is proposed to drive the division and movement of the endothelial cells of the growing tumor. Shown in cultured cells.
The dividing endothelium is the growing tumor seen in the skin.
Ulcers form while the tumor is growing. Why the skin over a growing hemangioma breaks down is not established in the sources cited.
A tumor of the eyelid can press on the eye and distort it, producing astigmatism, or cover the pupil. Either can leave the eye with poor vision.
The same tumor can grow in the wall of the airway below the vocal cords.
The same tumor can grow in the liver.
The vessels of large or numerous liver tumors can carry blood past the liver tissue.
The tumor tissue itself makes the enzyme.

edges.description: Fine dilated vessels are the commonest change left in the skin when the tumor has gone.

The shunted blood returns to the heart at once, so the heart must raise its output.
Thyroid hormone is destroyed in the tumor faster than it is made.

nodes.description: Poor vision in an eye that was not used properly in infancy. A hemangioma of the eyelid can cause it by distorting the eye, which produces astigmatism, or by covering the pupil. In a series of 96 children with a hemangioma around the eye, a tumor larger than 1 cm, a deep component and a site on the upper eyelid were each associated with astigmatism and with amblyopia. The abstract gives no rate, so no frequency is set.

nodes.description: The tumor of the skin. A precursor mark was present at birth in 65 per cent of a series of 30 infants with tumors of the face, and every tumor had appeared by three months in the cohort followed from birth. A superficial tumor is bright red; a deep one lies under skin of normal or bluish color and is soft enough to compress; a mixed one is both. Growth is fastest between five and a half and seven and a half weeks of age. The tumor reaches 80 per cent of its final size at about three months and has stopped growing by about five months in most children, although deep and segmental tumors grow for longer. In a review, 60 per cent of tumors are on the head and neck; in the cohort followed from birth most were on the trunk, and a fifth were small flat lesions that hardly grew.

nodes.description: The tumor contains multipotent stem cells, about 0.2 per cent of its cells, picked out by the marker CD133. Populations grown from single such cells formed human blood vessels within seven days of being implanted under the skin of immunodeficient mice, and the vessels carried GLUT1 and merosin, the markers of infantile hemangioma. The authors conclude that a stem cell, and not a mature endothelial cell, is the cell the tumor comes from. In culture, propranolol and its R enantiomer blocked the change of these stem cells into endothelial cells.

nodes.description: A beta-blocker taken by mouth, and the first-line treatment for a hemangioma that needs one. In the randomized trial of 456 infants, 3 mg per kg per day for six months cleared or nearly cleared the tumor in 60 per cent, against 4 per cent on placebo, and 88 per cent had improved by the fifth week. One in ten of those who responded needed treatment again. A meta-analysis of 18 studies estimated clearance at 95 per cent with propranolol, 43 per cent with oral corticosteroids and 6 per cent without treatment. The guideline dose is 2 to 3 mg per kg per day for at least six months. Low blood sugar, low blood pressure, a slow heart rate and bronchospasm are the known harms; in the trial they were infrequent. How the drug works is not settled (see the discussions).

nodes.description: In its growing phase the tumor is a dense mass of dividing endothelial cells that form capillaries. Endothelial cells cultured from growing hemangiomas are clonal, and they divide and move faster than normal endothelial cells. The endothelium stains strongly for the glucose transporter GLUT1 in every phase of the tumor, growing or shrinking: in a pathology study 139 of 143 hemangiomas were positive and none of 66 vascular malformations. GLUT1 is otherwise found in endothelium that forms a barrier between blood and tissue, as in the brain and the placenta, and the hemangioma shares three further markers with the vessels of the placenta.

nodes.description: The skin over the tumor breaks down in about one child in six seen at a specialist clinic: 173 of 1,096 children in the largest series. Ulcers form at a median age of four months, while the tumor is growing, and are commoner in large, mixed and segmental tumors and on the lower lip, the neck and the anogenital area. They can be painful and can scar. About two fifths of ulcerated tumors bled, rarely to a degree that mattered, and about one in six became infected.

evidence.reference_title: Multicenter prospective study of ulcerated hemangiomas.
evidence.snippet: One thousand ninety-six patients were enrolled, and 173 (15.8%) patients experienced ulceration.

evidence.reference_title: Multicenter prospective study of ulcerated hemangiomas.
evidence.snippet: Ulceration occurred at a median age of 4 months, most often during the proliferative phase.

evidence.reference_title: Multicenter prospective study of ulcerated hemangiomas.
evidence.snippet: Hemangiomas with ulcerations were more likely large, mixed clinical type, segmental morphologic type, and located on the lower lip, neck, or anogenital region.

evidence.reference_title: Multicenter prospective study of ulcerated hemangiomas.
evidence.snippet: Bleeding occurred in 41% of ulcerated lesions but was rarely of clinical significance. Infection occurred in 16%.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Infantile Hemangiomas.
evidence.snippet: These include IHs that may cause permanent scarring and disfigurement (eg, facial IHs), hepatic or airway IHs, and IHs with the potential for functional impairment (eg, periorbital IHs), ulceration (that may cause pain or scarring), and associated underlying abnormalities (eg, intracranial and aortic arch vascular abnormalities accompanying a large facial IH).

nodes.description: A hemangioma in the airway, typically below the vocal cords. It is rare: 13 of 761 children with hemangiomas at one vascular anomaly center had a subglottic one, and 1.6 per cent of 798 at another had a hemangioma of the airway. It is diagnosed at about four months, with noisy breathing in and out, a barking cough and breathlessness, and can be taken for croup. A segmental hemangioma of the lower face and neck, the beard area, is the warning sign: a third of the children who had one in the second series had a tumor of the airway. But in the first series more than half of the children with a subglottic tumor had no hemangioma of the skin at all.

evidence.reference_title: Subglottic hemangioma: Understanding the association with facial segmental hemangioma in a beard distribution.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of 761 cases of infantile hemangiomas demonstrated only 13 patients with subglottic hemangiomas (1.7%).

evidence.reference_title: Risk Factors for Airway Infantile Hemangioma.
evidence.snippet: This study included 798 children with an IH visiting our paediatric vascular anomaly unit between 1.1.2008 and 31.12.2017.

evidence.reference_title: Risk Factors for Airway Infantile Hemangioma.
evidence.snippet: An airway IH was diagnosed in 1.6% of the cohort. When a segmental beard distribution hemangioma was present, the risk for an airway IH was 33.3%, and when a non-beard distribution segmental hemangioma on the face or neck was observed, the risk was 11.5%.

evidence.reference_title: Subglottic hemangioma: Understanding the association with facial segmental hemangioma in a beard distribution.
evidence.snippet: Of those 13 patients, only 4 patients (30%) had BD while 2 patients (15%) had other cutaneous hemangiomas and 7 patients (55%) had no cutaneous hemangiomas.

evidence.reference_title: Update on infantile hemangioma.
evidence.snippet: Subglottic hemangiomas are diagnosed at mean age of 4 months, and patients present with progressive biphasic stridor, a barking cough, and dyspnea, and they may be misdiagnosed with congenital laryngeal stridor or infectious croup

nodes.description: Endothelial cells cultured from the hemangiomas of nine patients make little VEGFR1, the receptor that binds the growth factor VEGF without passing on a growth signal: its protein level was 10 to 20 per cent of that in control cells. The gene for VEGFR1 (FLT1) is switched on by the transcription factor NFAT, and NFAT is underactive in these cells because a pathway through beta-1 integrin, the integrin-like receptor TEM8 (ANTXR1) and VEGFR2 is underactive. Hemangioma tissue in the proliferating phase showed the same low ratio of VEGFR1 to VEGFR2 transcripts; involuting tissue did not.

evidence.reference_title: Suppressed NFAT-dependent VEGFR1 expression and constitutive VEGFR2 signaling in infantile hemangioma.
evidence.snippet: We show that expression of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (VEGFR1) in hemangioma endothelial cells (hemECs) and hemangioma tissue is markedly reduced compared to controls.

evidence.reference_title: Suppressed NFAT-dependent VEGFR1 expression and constitutive VEGFR2 signaling in infantile hemangioma.
evidence.snippet: The results showed that VEGFR1 protein levels in hemEC were only 10−20% of those in control cells

evidence.reference_title: Suppressed NFAT-dependent VEGFR1 expression and constitutive VEGFR2 signaling in infantile hemangioma.
evidence.snippet: In hemECs, transcription of the gene encoding VEGFR1 (FLT1) is dependent on nuclear factor of activated T cells (NFAT).

evidence.reference_title: Suppressed NFAT-dependent VEGFR1 expression and constitutive VEGFR2 signaling in infantile hemangioma.
evidence.snippet: Low VEGFR1 expression in hemECs is caused by reduced activity of a pathway involving beta1 integrin, the integrin-like receptor tumor endothelial marker-8 (TEM8), VEGFR2 and NFAT.

evidence.reference_title: Suppressed NFAT-dependent VEGFR1 expression and constitutive VEGFR2 signaling in infantile hemangioma.
evidence.snippet: real-time PCR showed COX-2/VEGFR2 and VEGFR1/VEGFR2 transcript ratios to be considerably lower in proliferating hemangioma tissue and hemEC than in HDMEC and other control endothelial cells, control tissues and involuting hemangioma tissue

nodes.description: Surgery is rarely the first treatment. It is used mainly to remove or reshape what the involuted tumor leaves behind. One study suggests considering it at about three and a half years of age, when most tumors have stopped improving.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Infantile Hemangiomas.
evidence.snippet: Surgery and/or laser treatment are most useful for the treatment of residual skin changes after involution and, less commonly, may be considered earlier to treat some IHs.

evidence.reference_title: Infantile hemangioma: clinical assessment of the involuting phase and implications for management.
evidence.snippet: Most infantile hemangiomas do not improve significantly after 3.5 years of age.

evidence.reference_title: Infantile hemangioma: clinical assessment of the involuting phase and implications for management.
evidence.snippet: Twenty-six percent of the cohort was treated with a corticosteroid during the proliferative phase and 87.6 percent underwent reconstruction for a residual deformity.

nodes.description: Corticosteroids by mouth were used before propranolol and are now kept for children who cannot take propranolol or do not respond to it. A randomized trial of 19 infants found prednisolone and propranolol similarly effective, but six of the eight infants on prednisolone left the trial early because of adverse events, and none of the 11 on propranolol. The meta-analysis estimated clearance at 43 per cent with oral corticosteroids.

evidence.reference_title: Update on infantile hemangioma.
evidence.snippet: Systemic corticosteroid therapy may be considered in IH patients in whom propranolol is contraindicated or ineffective

evidence.reference_title: Propranolol vs prednisolone for symptomatic proliferating infantile hemangiomas: a randomized clinical trial.
evidence.snippet: Phase 2, investigator-blinded, multi-institutional RCT conducted in 3 academic vascular anomalies clinics on 19 of 44 eligible infants aged between 2 weeks and 6 months.

evidence.reference_title: Propranolol vs prednisolone for symptomatic proliferating infantile hemangiomas: a randomized clinical trial.
evidence.snippet: Both medications show similar efficacy for reducing the area of symptomatic, proliferating IH. Although prednisolone showed a faster response rate, propranolol was better tolerated with significantly fewer severe AEs.

evidence.reference_title: Propranolol vs prednisolone for symptomatic proliferating infantile hemangiomas: a randomized clinical trial.
evidence.snippet: Early study withdrawal owing to AEs occurred in 6 (75%) of 8 patients in the prednisolone group but 0 of 11 propranolol-treated participants.

evidence.reference_title: Pharmacologic Interventions for Infantile Hemangioma: A Meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: Oral propranolol had the largest mean estimate of expected clearance (95%; 95% Bayesian credible interval [BCI]: 88%-99%) relative to oral corticosteroids (43%, 95% BCI: 21%-66%) and control (6%, 95% BCI: 1%-11%).

nodes.description: A beta-blocker applied to the skin. The guideline allows it for selected small, thin, superficial hemangiomas. A placebo-controlled trial of 69 infants younger than 60 days found no significant difference in clearance at 24 weeks, 11 infants in each group, and concluded that the benefit is limited when the drug is given that early.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Infantile Hemangiomas.
evidence.snippet: Topical timolol may be used to treat select small, thin, superficial IHs.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and Safety of Topical Timolol for the Treatment of Infantile Hemangioma in the Early Proliferative Stage: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
evidence.snippet: Of the 69 patients recruited, the mean (SD) age was 48.4 (10.6) days

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and Safety of Topical Timolol for the Treatment of Infantile Hemangioma in the Early Proliferative Stage: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
evidence.snippet: There were no significant differences between timolol and placebo for complete or nearly complete IH resolution at 24 weeks (n = 11 [42%] vs n = 11 [36%]; P = .37).

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and Safety of Topical Timolol for the Treatment of Infantile Hemangioma in the Early Proliferative Stage: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
evidence.snippet: In this randomized clinical trial, results demonstrated that topical timolol is well tolerated for the treatment of early proliferative IH but provides limited benefit in lesion resolution when given during the early proliferative stage.

nodes.description: Hemangioma tissue can make large amounts of type 3 iodothyronine deiodinase, the enzyme that inactivates thyroid hormone. When there is much tumor, as in multifocal or diffuse disease of the liver, the hormone is broken down faster than the thyroid gland can replace it. The condition is called consumptive hypothyroidism.
nodes.id: Type 3 Iodothyronine Deiodinase Activity in Tumor Tissue

evidence.reference_title: A Case of Consumptive Hypothyroidism in a 1-Month-Old Boy with Diffuse Infantile Hepatic Hemangiomas.
evidence.snippet: Consumptive hypothyroidism is a rare paraneoplastic syndrome characterized by excessive inactivation of the thyroid hormones due to increased type 3 iodothyronine deiodinase activity of tumors.

evidence.reference_title: Update on infantile hemangioma.
evidence.snippet: In cases of multiple or diffuse hepatic IHs, hypothyroidism can occur due to inactivation of the thyroid hormones by type 3 iodothyronine deiodinase in the IH tissue; therefore, thyroid function testing is required

evidence.reference_title: Consumptive hypothyroidism: a case report and review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Hepatic haemangioendotheliomata is capable of producing an excess of the thyroid hormone inactivating enzyme, type 3 iodothyronine deiodinase. The increased enzyme activity leads to rapid degradation of thyroid hormones, resulting in frank hypothyroidism.
